introduction:
House and Land Documents typically refer to Property Registration (Sale Deed, Gift Deed, etc.) in Andhra Pradesh. This is a mandatory process governed by the Registration Act, 1908, to ensure legal transfer of ownership and protect against future property disputes.

The registration is managed by the Registration and Stamps Department, AP (IGRS AP), and requires a combination of online pre-registration and physical biometric execution at the Sub-Registrar Office (SRO).
quickFacts:
Important to Know
  • Official Portal: IGRS AP (registration.ap.gov.in)
  • System Name: CARD PRIME / PRIMME (Property Registration Integration Mutation Made Easy).
  • Total Cost (Approx): ~7.5% of the property market value (or consideration value, whichever is higher).
    • Stamp Duty: 5%
    • Registration Fee: 1%
    • Transfer Duty: 1.5%
  • Time Taken: 1–3 days (often completed on the same day of the appointment).
  • Key Requirement: Presence of Buyer, Seller, and two witnesses at the Sub-Registrar Office (SRO) is mandatory.
documentsRequired:
Documents Required

Note: You must carry the original documents and one set of photocopies to the office.
Personal & Identity Proofs
  • Proof of Identity (Buyer & Seller): Aadhaar Card (mandatory), PAN Card.
  • Proof of Address: Aadhaar, Passport, or Voter ID.
  • Photographs: 2 Passport-sized photos of both Buyer and Seller.
  • Witnesses: Two witnesses with their ID proofs (Aadhaar).
Property Documents
  • Draft Sale Deed: The unsigned legal document containing sale details.
  • Encumbrance Certificate (EC): Proof that the property has no legal dues (usually for the last 13–30 years).
  • Link Documents: Previous sale deeds establishing the chain of ownership.
  • Property Tax Receipts: Latest tax payment receipt (from the seller).
  • Market Value Certificate: Can be obtained online to verify the government-fixed rate.
  • Pattadar Passbook: For agricultural land.
onlineApplication:
Method 1: Online Application (Public Data Entry via PRIMME)

The Andhra Pradesh government uses the PRIMME (Public Data Entry) system, which allows you to enter data and pay fees from home to save time at the office.

Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Step 1: Visit the Portal: Go to the official website (registration.ap.gov.in) and select "Public Data Entry" or "PRIMME".
  2. Step 2: Create Document:
    • Login (or register) using your Mobile Number/Email.
    • Select "New Document" and choose the transaction type (e.g., Sale Deed).
    • Enter details of the Seller (Executant), Buyer (Claimant), and Property (District, Mandal, Survey No.).
  3. Step 3: Upload & Edit:
    • Enter details of the Link Documents (previous registration numbers).
    • The system acts as a "Do-It-Yourself" drafter, allowing you to select standard legal clauses or upload your own draft.
  4. Step 4: Pay Fees:
    • Calculate the Stamp Duty and Registration Fees using the site's calculator.
    • Pay the amount online via Net Banking/UPI/Debit Card through the portal.
    • Save the Payment Receipt/Challan.
  5. Step 5: Book Slot:
    • Once data is saved, click on "Slot Booking".
    • Choose your jurisdictional Sub-Registrar Office (SRO), date, and time.
    • Download the Acknowledgement/Appointment Slip.
offlineApplication:
Method 2: Offline / Assisted Process

If you are not comfortable using the online portal yourself, you can follow the traditional "offline" route, which is now an assisted process.

Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Hire a Document Writer/Scribe: Visit the Sub-Registrar Office (SRO) area. There are licensed document writers or advocates nearby.
  2. Drafting: They will draft the Sale Deed on valid Non-Judicial Stamp Paper (or use the e-stamping facility) based on your agreement.
  3. Data Entry: The document writer will perform the "Public Data Entry" (mentioned in Method 1) on your behalf to generate the necessary slip.
  4. Fee Payment: You can pay the Stamp Duty and Registration fees via Bank Challan (at designated banks like SBI) or Demand Draft (DD) if online payment is not preferred.
  5. Visit SRO: The writer will arrange the file with all documents and accompany you to the Sub-Registrar Office for the registration.
afterApplying:
After Applying (At the Office & Post-Registration)

Whether you applied online or offline, you must physically visit the SRO on your appointment date:

  1. Step 1: Check-in: Present your Appointment Slip and original documents to the officer at the front desk.
  2. Step 2: Verification: The Sub-Registrar will verify the ID proofs, the payment challan, and the property details (checking for prohibited lands under Section 22A).
  3. Step 3: Biometrics:
    • Photos: The officer will take digital photos of the Buyer and Seller.
    • Fingerprints: Thumb impressions (and potentially iris scans) will be collected.
    • Signatures: Both parties and the two witnesses must sign the deed in front of the officer.
  4. Step 4: Completion: The Registrar will approve the registration. You will be given a receipt.
  5. Step 5: Document Collection:
    • The registered Sale Deed is scanned and uploaded to the central server.
    • You can typically collect the original registered document within 24 hours (sometimes 1 hour) from the dispatch section.
  6. Step 6: Mutation (Name Change):
    • Agricultural Land: Often triggers an automatic mutation request to the Revenue Department.
    • Non-Agricultural: You must apply for mutation separately at the local Municipal/Mandal office or via the Meebhoomi portal to officially change the name in revenue records.
